options.plan: Upstream release 26.8.0; commercial support not assessed
options.region: Operator-selected hosting; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Native OIDC/SAML clients and configurable inbound realm SCIM; no third-party extensions or outbound bridge

conditions: Register an OIDC client and enable Standard Flow for authorization-code login.
Configure exact redirect URIs, client authentication and the intended PKCE policy; documentation support does not verify a deployment.
This assertion concerns downstream application clients, not upstream enterprise federation or every authentication-control policy.

evidence.summary: The 26.8.0 source documentation describes configurable OIDC clients, an authorization-code Standard Flow switch, client authentication and a selectable PKCE method.

conditions: Register a SAML client and configure its application endpoints, bindings, signatures and keys.
A native downstream SAML application does not establish compatibility with a particular upstream Okta or Entra ID tenant.

evidence.summary: Release-pinned documentation describes SAML application client registration, POST/Redirect bindings and configurable signing and encryption. This is not a tested SAML integration.

conditions: Make the native SCIM server feature available and enable the SCIM API for the intended realm.
Use an authorized confidential service-account client with operation-specific permissions and the exact realm SCIM audience.
The scope is inbound realm provisioning; SaaS records, permissions, local sessions and any outbound bridge require separate integration and tests.

evidence.summary: The release-pinned SCIM chapter links native user/group lifecycle, per-realm enablement and bearer-token authorization documentation. Endpoint support does not prove application-side lifecycle enforcement.

conditions: Use the enabled, authorized native realm SCIM Groups interface; group claims alone are not provisioning.
Manage group members through PATCH, not Groups POST or PUT; member entries are users.
Organization-group memberships require the Organization API rather than this SCIM membership path.
Verify the consuming application's membership mapping and authorization updates independently.

evidence.summary: The 26.8.0 documentation describes realm SCIM group CRUD and PATCH-based user membership. It excludes organization-group membership management and membership writes in Groups POST/PUT.
